transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hello, Doctor. I'm Alejandro, and I'm here because I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop. It has become a real struggle for me lately.
Do you eat large amounts of food in a short time, especially at night, and feel unable to stop once you start?

Yes, that is exactly what happens. In just an hour or two, I will eat a whole pot of arroz con pollo, bread, and ice cream straight from the carton. It feels like a switch goes off in my brain and even when I tell myself "Alejandro, basta," my hands just keep piling food on the plate until it is all gone.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?

No, I don't do any of those things at all. I have never made myself vomit, taken laxatives, or tried to do excessive exercise after these episodes. I just end up sitting there feeling heavy and incredibly guilty.
Do you often feel down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, especially around the time of these eating episodes?

No, I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed most of the day. It is more that I feel very restless and worried about my heart health, and then deeply ashamed about my eating habits after these episodes happen.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen while you're fully awake and aware, or do you sometimes not remember them clearly, like you were on 'autopilot' or even partially asleep?

I am completely awake and remember everything clearly; I'm definitely not asleep or forgetting what happened. It just feels like a physical switch flips in my brain and my hands go on autopilot, but I am fully conscious and aware of what I'm doing the entire time.
Do you ever eat during the night while only partially awake, such as right after waking up from sleep, without full control or memory of the episode?
No, that never happens to me. I am always fully awake and I remember everything I eat perfectly. I never get out of bed in the middle of the night to eat while asleep or half-awake.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was F50.8, which refers to other specified eating disorders. The patient describes recurrent episodes of night eating with a sense of loss of control, full awareness during the episodes, and no compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise. The absence of nocturnal eating during partial arousal from sleep (ruling out sleep-related eating disorder) and the presence of full recall and wakefulness support that this is not a parasomnia. There is also no evidence of depressed mood as a core feature, making depressive disorders less likely contributors. The clinical picture aligns with a specified eating disorder that does not meet full criteria for binge eating disorder, bulimia nervosa, or sleep-related eating disorder. Therefore, the candidate remains F50.8, as it encompasses atypical presentations such as night eating syndrome or similar conditions with clinically significant eating disturbances that do not fulfill criteria for other specific diagnoses.
